title: Environmental Sampling and Analysis
description: Treats environmental data as evidence produced through sampling design, field protocols, laboratory methods, QA/QC, and defensible interpretation—covering water, soil, sediment, air, and biological matrices from study design through regulatory reporting.

topics.title: Environmental Sampling and Analysis as Measurement Practice
topics.description: Frame environmental data as evidence produced through sampling design, field protocols, laboratory methods, and defensible interpretation.

children.title: From question to defensible evidence
children.description: Students learn that environmental analysis begins with a management or scientific question, then works backward to evidence requirements.

children.title: Matrices and analyte classes
children.description: This subtopic builds the vocabulary for what is sampled and what is measured.

children.title: Field-to-lab workflow
children.description: Students see sampling and analysis as one continuous quality-controlled chain.

topics.title: Study Design, Data Quality Objectives, and Site Selection
topics.description: Design sampling programs around clear decisions, target populations, spatial patterns, and data quality needs.

children.title: Data quality objectives
children.description: Students learn to specify the required quality of data before collecting samples.

children.title: Spatial sampling design
children.description: This subtopic addresses where samples should be collected to represent environmental conditions.

children.title: Temporal design
children.description: Students plan when and how often to sample dynamic environmental systems.

topics.title: Field Safety, Permits, Ethics, and Logistics
topics.description: Plan fieldwork that protects people, communities, sites, samples, and legal compliance.

children.title: Field safety planning
children.description: Students learn to anticipate field hazards and write practical safety procedures.

children.title: Permits and access
children.description: This subtopic covers legal and practical permissions for environmental sampling.

children.title: Ethics and community accountability
children.description: Students learn that sampling can affect communities, sites, and public trust.

topics.title: Sampling Statistics, Representativeness, and Uncertainty
topics.description: Use statistical thinking to manage heterogeneity, replication, detection limits, and uncertainty.

children.title: Representativeness and heterogeneity
children.description: Students learn why environmental samples often vary strongly across space and time.

children.title: Replication and power
children.description: This subtopic connects sample number to confidence in environmental conclusions.

children.title: Uncertainty sources
children.description: Students separate sampling uncertainty, analytical uncertainty, and interpretation uncertainty.

topics.title: Water Sampling: Surface Water, Groundwater, and Wastewater
topics.description: Collect water samples using protocols matched to hydrology, analytes, and regulatory goals.

children.title: Surface-water sampling
children.description: Students learn protocols for rivers, lakes, wetlands, and stormwater.

children.title: Groundwater sampling
children.description: This subtopic covers well purging, stabilization, and aquifer-specific procedures.

children.title: Wastewater and process samples
children.description: Students learn how sampling differs in engineered systems and regulated discharges.

topics.title: Soil, Sediment, and Solid-Matrix Sampling
topics.description: Sample heterogeneous solids while controlling depth, grain size, contamination, and preservation effects.

children.title: Soil sampling strategies
children.description: Students learn how depth, location, and compositing affect soil data.

children.title: Sediment sampling
children.description: This subtopic addresses aquatic solids and depositional environments.

children.title: Solid sample preparation
children.description: Students learn preparation steps that can change or preserve analytical meaning.

topics.title: Air Monitoring and Atmospheric Sampling
topics.description: Measure gases, vapors, particulates, and exposure-relevant air pollutants with appropriate instruments and designs.

children.title: Air pollutant categories
children.description: Students distinguish major air analytes and why each requires different sampling methods.

children.title: Active and passive sampling
children.description: This subtopic covers how air samples are captured over time.

children.title: Continuous monitoring
children.description: Students learn how automated air monitoring creates high-frequency environmental data.

topics.title: Biological Monitoring and Bioassessment
topics.description: Use organisms, tissues, communities, and biomarkers as evidence of environmental condition and exposure.

children.title: Indicator organisms and communities
children.description: Students use biological responses as integrative measures of environmental condition.

children.title: Tissue and biomarker sampling
children.description: This subtopic links organisms to contaminant exposure and biological effect.

children.title: eDNA and modern biomonitoring
children.description: Students learn emerging molecular approaches for detecting organisms and biodiversity.

topics.title: Sample Preservation, Handling, Transport, and Chain of Custody
topics.description: Protect sample integrity from collection through laboratory receipt and legal/regulatory documentation.

children.title: Containers and preservation
children.description: Students match containers and preservation to analytes and methods.

children.title: Transport and holding times
children.description: This subtopic prevents degradation, volatilization, and invalid results.

children.title: Documentation and legal defensibility
children.description: Students learn documentation practices that make data auditable.

topics.title: Field Measurements and Sensor-Based Monitoring
topics.description: Use in situ instruments, probes, loggers, and calibration checks to collect high-quality field data.

children.title: Water-quality field probes
children.description: Students collect immediate measurements that can change after sampling.

children.title: Field meters and calibration checks
children.description: This subtopic builds habits for trustworthy field instrumentation.

children.title: Deployable sensors
children.description: Students learn strengths and limitations of long-term automated monitoring.

topics.title: Wet Chemistry and Classical Environmental Analyses
topics.description: Apply titrimetric, gravimetric, colorimetric, and nutrient methods to common environmental measurements.

children.title: Basic water-quality analyses
children.description: Students learn common bench methods for routine environmental parameters.

children.title: Nutrients and oxygen demand
children.description: This subtopic focuses on eutrophication and organic pollution indicators.

children.title: Solids and gravimetric methods
children.description: Students learn mass-based measurements that remain central in water and wastewater work.

topics.title: Instrumental Analysis: Spectroscopy, Chromatography, and Mass Spectrometry
topics.description: Choose instrumental methods for metals, nutrients, organics, trace contaminants, and complex mixtures.

children.title: Metals and elemental analysis
children.description: Students choose methods for trace metals and elemental contaminants.

children.title: Organic contaminant analysis
children.description: This subtopic covers separations and detectors for complex organic mixtures.

children.title: Emerging contaminants
children.description: Students learn why some analytes require specialized methods and interpretation.

topics.title: QA/QC, Calibration, Blanks, Duplicates, and Method Validation
topics.description: Build quality systems that detect contamination, bias, drift, precision problems, and method failure.

children.title: Quality control samples
children.description: Students learn how QC samples diagnose contamination, precision, bias, and recovery.

children.title: Calibration and validation
children.description: This subtopic covers how laboratories prove methods are working.

children.title: Data quality assessment
children.description: Students learn to judge whether a dataset meets its project objectives.

topics.title: Data Validation, Reporting Limits, and Environmental Data Interpretation
topics.description: Evaluate whether data are usable and interpret results against standards, background, and risk context.

children.title: Non-detects and censored data
children.description: Students learn to interpret results below detection or reporting limits responsibly.

children.title: Validation qualifiers
children.description: This subtopic explains flags that communicate data usability.

children.title: Comparing data to criteria
children.description: Students connect analytical results to standards, background, and risk.

topics.title: Geospatial, Time-Series, and Regulatory Reporting Workflows
topics.description: Integrate field/lab data with maps, metadata, databases, standards, and professional reporting requirements.

children.title: Spatial data integration
children.description: Students learn to map samples and interpret environmental patterns.

children.title: Time-series interpretation
children.description: This subtopic covers monitoring datasets that change through time.

children.title: Professional reporting
children.description: Students learn the structure and expectations of environmental data deliverables.

topics.title: Integrated Field-to-Lab Capstone Project
topics.description: Synthesize sampling design, field collection, lab analysis, QA/QC, interpretation, and communication in a complete dataset submission.

children.title: Sampling and analysis plan
children.description: Students synthesize course concepts into a professional plan.

children.title: Dataset production
children.description: This subtopic moves from plan to actual samples, results, and QC review.

children.title: Interpretation and communication
children.description: Students turn environmental measurements into defensible conclusions.
